analysis.title: From AI To KO: BofA Says The Flight-To-Safety Has Become A Bubble Of Its Own
key_insights: BofA's Global Equity Volatility Insights note 'Defensives can bubble too' finds the highest US Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) readings are now in healthcare and consumer staples, not semis.
Last week the Nasdaq fell more than 5% and the SOX more than 10%, the worst week for both since April 2025. The SOX fell eight straight sessions, matching its longest losing streak since 2006.

BofA calls the selloff a largely positioning-driven hiccup on the edges of the AI trade. CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) fell 20-25% on the week, far more than their betas implied, while Mag8 megacaps tracked their betas.

The 5-day spread between S&P defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) and tech blew out to levels seen only during the dotcom bubble. BofA says US equities rotate sharply under stress rather than rupture.

On Friday Oct 16 the VIX rose about 6 points intraday toward 22 and closed the week at 19.99, up from 14.84 a week earlier. The move exceeded the expected reaction to a roughly 1.5% S&P drop, in an index that had gone 53 sessions without a 1% decline until the prior Wednesday.

BofA calls the VIX spike a positioning-driven 'mini-fragility event'. Tell 1: the VIX move was too large relative to the SPX decline, after weak VIX-SPX beta in recent weeks. Tell 2: the VIX vs SPX 1-month ATM vol spread widened as downside tail vol drove the VIX, as in Feb 2018 and Aug 2024.

Dealer short gamma in the VIX complex (ETPs plus options) going into Friday was larger than at any point outside the top 4% of readings since 2014. Investors monetizing VIX call hedges dampened the spike while dealer re-hedging amplified it, and the amplifiers won.
Bloomberg cites a BofA estimate that a 10-point shock in front-month VIX futures could force dealers to buy roughly 90% of a day's VIX futures volume to stay delta-neutral.
BRI is a price-based 0-to-1 score built from returns, realized volatility, momentum and convexity. BofA uses 0.8 as its danger line: seven of eight historical bubbles peaked above it.

US healthcare had the highest BRI among BofA's global indices, US sectors, commodities and crypto, near 0.8. Energy and staples were each about 0.67 and tech about 0.5. Nasdaq, Nikkei and Kospi BRIs retreated (chart-read, approximate).

The 'US Pharma Hyperscalers' custom basket reads 0.75. US cybersecurity is at 0.83 and Brazil's election basket is highest at 0.90. Pharma had the biggest weekly jump in bubble risk among popular themes.

The S&P 500 stocks with the highest BRI are Moderna (MRNA), Coca-Cola (KO), Revvity (RVTY) and Zebra (ZBRA). Amgen, Merck, Agilent, Thermo Fisher, Quest Diagnostics and Smucker are also in the top 25, and healthcare is about half the list.

Positioning: Morgan Stanley's prime book showed hedge fund healthcare exposure in the 3rd percentile of the past year, and Goldman said funds de-grossed the sector four straight weeks. Privorotsky noted quality rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with an RSI of 83.

BofA says the froth is localized. Only 13 S&P stocks have a BRI above 0.8, or 2.8% of index market cap, versus 50-100 stocks and 20-40% of market cap at the dotcom peak. A high BRI is a cue to buy protection, not a sell signal.

BofA's trade view: XLP and XLV implied vols are about the 20th percentile versus XLK vol, cheap against their own realized vol, while XLK vol screens rich. Bloomberg says staples hedging costs fell more than any other sector last week.

BofA recommends two relative-value put trades, both about 25-delta and for a small credit: XLP vs XLK, and XLV vs XLK. For those wary of naked XLK puts into earnings, FOMC and the midterms, it suggests XLK put spreads as the funding leg.

Longer-dated hedge: NDX Sep27 max lookback puts contingent on 10Y rates falling. Last week's NDX -5.5% and 10Y -16bps supported BofA's view that an AI unwind resembles 2000-01, with equities and rates both down.
Goldman's healthcare desk noted that Monday's TMT/AI bounce drove defensive underperformance, so the two sides of the rotation trade like a single toggle.

ZeroHedge's own view: if last week was more than a hiccup, the AI financing squeeze (hyperscaler CDS at record wides) could hit defensives too, as in a true liquidation investors sell what they still own.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA argues the tech selloff was a positioning-driven hiccup, and that dispersion inside tech and damage already done limit the risk of continued rotation, so tech bounces and defensives deflate.
